scope_note: Amazon review logs dominate every split (8 of 10 discovery logs, 12 of 14 holdout logs). A 'confirmed' verdict therefore means 'confirmed on Amazon-dominated logs'; the non-Amazon means are reported separately. Nine of the holdout logs were used in the earlier tracking study (they chose the baseline half-life 2); only the 5 fresh Amazon categories are completely new.

hypotheses.name: plain recent window beats decay
hypotheses.statement: Summing only the last 3 rounds gives a better list than the decayed sum with half-life 2.
hypotheses.prediction: Fails: a hard cut-off throws away useful older answers (expected kill).

hypotheses.name: rising items
hypotheses.statement: Adding extra weight to items whose recent share is above their older share gives a better list.
hypotheses.prediction: Helps only where many new items enter the top 100; net effect on Amazon about zero.

hypotheses.name: two timescales
hypotheses.statement: Half recent (h=1) plus half long-run (all history) gives a better list than the single half-life 2.
hypotheses.prediction: Fails on Amazon (single timescale already best), may help in the other logs.

hypotheses.name: cap what each person reports
hypotheses.statement: Letting each person report at most 3 rows per round loses less than 0.01 NDCG.
hypotheses.prediction: Holds: heavy users add little new information (needed for privacy and bandwidth).

hypotheses.name: ask every round, not in batches
hypotheses.statement: Spending the same budget on twice as many people every second round is worse than n people every round by 0.01 or more.
hypotheses.prediction: Holds: staleness hurts more than sampling noise.

hypotheses.name: minimum count per item
hypotheses.statement: Dropping items reported only once in a round loses less than 0.01 NDCG.
hypotheses.prediction: Holds: one-off reports are noise (needed for k-anonymity-style privacy).

gates.unit: Everything is judged SEPARATELY for each n (people per round) on the logs eligible at that n; at least min_logs_per_n logs are required, otherwise that n is 'not testable'. A missing expected cell makes the whole stage INCOMPLETE (no verdict).
gates.screen: n = 30 and 100, 6 draws, own draws. Keep a hypothesis if its primary rule moves the right way at any tested n: superiority mean diff > +0.005; noninferiority mean diff > -0.01; dominated mean diff < -0.005.
gates.full: PASS at an n: superiority = mean diff >= +0.01 AND diff>0 in >=70% of logs AND one-sided t lower bound at level alpha/(family*3) > 0; noninferiority = t lower bound of mean diff > -0.01 AND worst log diff > -0.03; dominated = mean diff <= -0.01 AND diff<0 in >=70% of logs AND t upper bound < 0. A hypothesis advances if it PASSES at one or more n.
gates.holdout: same rule at level alpha/3 for each n, plus the mean diff on the fresh logs alone must have the same sign (superiority > 0; noninferiority > -0.01; dominated < 0). CONFIRMED only at the n values that PASS both discovery and holdout.

h7.statement: Setting the half-life from a log's new-item share (line fitted leave-one-log-out) gives lower mean NDCG regret than a fixed half-life of 2.
h7.prediction: Fails: Amazon is almost flat at h*=2, so the line cannot beat the fixed rule there.
h7.amendment: The first registered wording ('better in at least 70% of logs') was found unreachable by construction (the rule picks h=2 in most logs, so ties count against it) after the offline numbers had already been printed in a smoke test (0 of 19 logs better, mean regret 0.0152 vs 0.0105). The criterion was changed to mean regret. Both are reported; H7 is therefore not a blind test.

h8.statement: The best half-life is a calendar length. (a) At 90 windows, among the logs flagged 'same in days' whose calendar-predicted and rounds-predicted grid points differ, the NDCG at the calendar-predicted half-life beats the NDCG at the rounds-predicted half-life in at least 70% of logs (paired over draws). (b) On the fresh Amazon logs at 30 windows, the NDCG at the half-life nearest 534 days is within 0.005 of the best grid NDCG in at least 70% of logs.
h8.prediction: Holds for Amazon; the 45-window run is reported but cannot separate the two rules.
h8.note: amazon-industrial-and-scientific is eligible only at n=30, so (b) has about 4 logs.
